senses.definition: An artwork made by attaching pieces of paper, cloth, or other material to a surface.
senses.example: The class made a collage out of old maps and scraps of paper.

senses.definition: To gather things together or get something that is waiting for you.
senses.example: We collect fallen leaves for an art project.

senses.definition: To gather a certain kind of thing over time because you like it.
senses.example: My uncle likes to collect old stamps.

senses.definition: A group of things that have been gathered together.
senses.example: My aunt has a collection of old postcards.

senses.definition: A place controlled by another country, often after people from that country settle there.
senses.example: Massachusetts was once a British colony.

senses.definition: The way light makes something look red, blue, green, or another shade.
senses.example: Yellow was the brightest color in the mural.

senses.definition: A tall upright part that helps hold up a building or stands by itself.
senses.example: A stone column stood at each corner of the porch.

senses.definition: A vertical list or group of words, numbers, or pictures.
senses.example: Find the first column of the chart.

senses.definition: To find or meet something or someone by chance.
senses.example: You might come across a sketch Dad drew between the pages of that book.

senses.definition: To think of something that solves a problem or adds an idea.
senses.example: We had to come up with a way to carry six cups without spilling them.

senses.definition: A story, play, or show meant to be funny, or humor used as entertainment.
senses.example: Our class watched a short comedy about a lost hat.

senses.definition: An icy object that travels around the Sun and can grow glowing tails of gas and dust as it warms up.
senses.example: The comet grew a bright tail as it drew near the Sun.

senses.definition: A feeling of being at ease, or something that makes a hard time easier.
senses.example: My favorite story brought me comfort when I was sick.

senses.definition: To help someone feel less worried, sad, or hurt.
senses.example: A quiet word helped comfort my friend.

senses.definition: A punctuation mark that separates words or parts of a sentence.
senses.example: I added a comma between the first two things on the list.

senses.definition: An order that tells someone or something what to do.
senses.example: The computer followed the command to open a new page.

senses.definition: To give an order or be in charge of a group.
senses.example: The captain commanded the crew to prepare for the next stop.

senses.definition: Seen or happening often.
senses.example: A robin is a common sight in our neighborhood.

senses.definition: Used or shared by two or more people or things.
senses.example: Everyone in the room worked toward a common goal.

senses.definition: A bottom number that can be used for two or more fractions without changing their values.
senses.example: Six is a common denominator for one half and one third because they can be written as three sixths and two sixths.

senses.definition: People who live in the same area or share an interest or way of life.
senses.example: Our community organized a cleanup in the park.

senses.definition: A rule that says swapping two numbers being added or multiplied leaves the answer the same.
senses.example: By the commutative property, five times eight equals eight times five.

senses.definition: To look at two or more things to see how they are alike or different.
senses.example: We compared the two maps to see which streets had changed.

senses.definition: A tool that helps you find directions, often with a needle that lines up with Earth’s magnetic field.
senses.example: We checked the compass before turning toward the trail.

senses.definition: A tool with two joined arms that can be used to draw circles.
senses.example: I used a compass to draw the biggest wheel on my picture.

senses.definition: To try to win something that others are also trying to win.
senses.example: Six teams will compete on Saturday.

senses.definition: To tell someone that you are unhappy about something.
senses.example: A few riders complained about the long wait.

senses.definition: Finished or having every part it needs.
senses.example: The puzzle is complete now that we found the last piece.

senses.definition: To finish doing or making something.
senses.example: We need one more drawing to complete the poster.

senses.definition: A person who creates a piece of music.
senses.example: The composer wrote a different part for each instrument.

senses.definition: A dark mixture formed after scraps from plants and other living things break down.
senses.example: The finished compost was mixed with soil near the flowers.

senses.definition: A substance made of atoms from at least two different elements chemically joined in a fixed proportion.
senses.example: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

senses.definition: A way to store or send information in less space than it took before.
senses.example: Compression made my photo file smaller.

senses.definition: An event where people play or sing music for others to hear.
senses.example: Our class went to a concert in the park.

senses.definition: The change from a gas to a liquid. It can happen when water vapor touches something cooler.
senses.example: Condensation made tiny drops on the outside of my cold glass.

senses.definition: Something that has to be true for a rule or action to apply.
senses.example: Our game ends if one player reaches ten points. Reaching ten points is the condition.

senses.definition: How something is doing or what kind of shape it is in.
senses.example: The bicycle was old but still in good condition.

senses.definition: In a program, instructions that are used only if a particular test has the right result.
senses.example: The game uses a conditional to check whether I reached the end.

senses.definition: The movement of heat or electricity through something, such as through a metal spoon.
senses.example: The spoon handle warmed by conduction after the bowl of the spoon touched the soup.

senses.definition: A material that lets electricity or heat move through it easily.
senses.example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.

senses.definition: A person who leads a group of musicians as they play or sing.
senses.example: We watched the conductor for the signal to start playing.

senses.definition: A person who helps run a train and may check passengers’ tickets.
senses.example: The conductor announced the next stop.

senses.definition: A solid shape with a round or other closed base and sides that narrow to a single point.
senses.example: The paper party hat looked like a cone.

senses.definition: A cell in the eye that helps you see colors and details in enough light.
senses.example: Different cone cells can respond more strongly to different colors of light.

senses.definition: Feeling sure that you can do something or that something is true.
senses.example: I felt confident that I could read the poem aloud.

senses.definition: To make it hard for someone to understand or tell things apart.
senses.example: The missing sign may confuse people looking for the exit.

senses.definition: To mix up two things and think one is the other.
senses.example: I confuse those two street names because they sound alike.

senses.definition: To join two or more things or make a link between them.
senses.example: Connect the dots to make a picture.

senses.definition: The basic rules that describe how a government is organized and what it can do. A constitution can also protect people’s rights.
senses.example: The United States Constitution sets out the jobs of the three branches of the national government.

senses.definition: One of the largest land areas into which people divide Earth. Different maps sometimes group them in different ways.
senses.example: A map can show the continent of Africa and the countries within it.

senses.definition: To keep doing something or to start it again after a pause.
senses.example: We will continue the story tomorrow.

senses.definition: A line on a map that joins places at the same height.
senses.example: One contour line curved all the way around the hill.

senses.definition: To guide what something does or keep it within limits.
senses.example: These buttons control the fan speed.

senses.definition: The power to guide something, or a device that lets you do it.
senses.example: The volume control is on the right side of the screen.

senses.definition: The way a gas or liquid carries heat as it moves from place to place.
senses.example: Convection carried warmer water toward the top of the pot.

senses.definition: A talk in which people take turns sharing ideas or information.
senses.example: We had a conversation about what to paint on the sign.

senses.definition: To use heat to prepare food for eating.
senses.example: Please cook the carrots until they are soft enough to cut.

senses.definition: A person who prepares food and meals.
senses.example: The cook served soup and bread at noon.

senses.definition: To work together or help someone carry out a plan.
senses.example: We had to cooperate to move the heavy table.

senses.definition: One of the numbers that describes the position of a point on a map or grid.
senses.example: The first coordinate in (5, 2) tells how far right to go.

senses.definition: A thing made to match another thing, or one of several printed versions of the same work.
senses.example: I borrowed a copy of the story from the library.

senses.definition: To make something like another thing or repeat what it says or does.
senses.example: Copy the figures into your notebook before you add them.

senses.definition: A small ocean animal with a soft, tube-shaped body. Many corals live in groups and make hard structures that can build up into reefs.
senses.example: Fish sheltered among the branches of a coral.

senses.definition: A pinkish orange color.
senses.example: I mixed pink and orange paint to make coral.

senses.definition: Right or matching the facts or rules.
senses.example: Three is the correct answer to the first question.

senses.definition: To fix an error or tell someone what the right answer is.
senses.example: We used a spare line to correct our spelling.

senses.definition: Damage to a material after it reacts with substances around it, such as air or moisture.
senses.example: A coat of paint can protect a steel bridge from corrosion.

senses.definition: The amount of money, time, or effort that you must give up to get or do something.
senses.example: The cost of the bus ride was one dollar.

senses.definition: To require payment or make someone give something up.
senses.example: How much will that book cost?

senses.definition: A weight used to balance another weight or make it easier to move around.
senses.example: A counterweight balances much of the weight of the elevator car.

senses.definition: The strength to do something even if it feels scary or hard.
senses.example: It took courage to ask for help in front of the group.

senses.definition: A child of your parent’s sibling, or a more distant person in the same family.
senses.example: My cousin visits us every July.

senses.definition: To put something over another thing or hide it from view.
senses.example: Cover the bowl so the food stays fresh.

senses.definition: To include or deal with a subject.
senses.example: The second chapter will cover clouds and rain.

senses.definition: Something that goes over another thing to protect, hide, or close it.
senses.example: The cover of the book had a picture of a train.

senses.definition: A narrow split or opening in a surface.
senses.example: A tiny ant came out of a crack in the wall.

senses.definition: To split, make a sharp noise, or solve a hard problem.
senses.example: I managed to crack the code before the timer beeped.

senses.definition: An activity or skill that uses your hands to make something.
senses.example: Paper cutting was the craft we practiced today.

senses.definition: A vehicle made to travel on water, in the air, or in space.
senses.example: The small craft sailed away from the floating dock.

senses.definition: To make something with care or skill.
senses.example: We crafted the little chair from sticks.

senses.definition: A round hollow, often made where something struck a surface or around the opening of a volcano.
senses.example: The large crater on the Moon has high sides.

senses.definition: A marked line on a cricket pitch used to show a position or boundary in play.
senses.example: The batter ran past the crease before the ball reached the wicket.

senses.definition: To make something new or cause something to exist.
senses.example: We used paper scraps to create a city map.

senses.definition: Praise for doing or helping with something.
senses.example: Our teacher gave Lina credit for drawing the map.

senses.definition: An arrangement that lets you receive something now and pay for it later.
senses.example: The store allowed the family to buy the chairs on credit.

senses.definition: To say who helped, made something, or deserves praise.
senses.example: The sign credits local students for its artwork.

senses.definition: A gradual increase in loudness in music.
senses.example: A slow crescendo took the tune from quiet to loud.

senses.definition: Growing different kinds of crops on the same land in a planned order, often to keep soil healthy and reduce pests.
senses.example: As part of their crop rotation, the farmers planted beans in a field that had grown corn the year before.

senses.definition: A large group of people in one place.
senses.example: A crowd gathered to watch the show.

senses.definition: To fill a place or press close together in it.
senses.example: Please don’t crowd around the doorway.

senses.definition: A small piece of bread, cake, or another food that breaks off easily.
senses.example: A crumb fell onto my sleeve.

senses.definition: A part of a vehicle made to bend in a crash to help protect the people inside.
senses.example: A car can have a crumple zone near its front end.

senses.definition: To make a loud, crisp sound by chewing, crushing, or stepping on something.
senses.example: Dry leaves crunch beneath my boots.

senses.definition: A crisp sound made when something is chewed or crushed.
senses.example: I heard the crunch of gravel under the tires.

senses.definition: The firm outer part of bread, a pie, or something similar.
senses.example: The bread had a crisp crust.

senses.definition: The outer, rocky layer of Earth or a similar body.
senses.example: A mountain rises from Earth’s crust.

senses.definition: A solid with particles arranged in a pattern that repeats throughout it.
senses.example: Under a magnifier, a crystal of table salt looked like a tiny cube.

senses.definition: The space taken up by a cube whose edges are all one unit long.
senses.example: If one cube holds one cubic unit of space, three cubes hold three cubic units.

senses.definition: Broken or crushed glass gathered for use when making new glass.
senses.example: The glass plant mixed clean cullet with sand and its other supplies.

senses.definition: A small container for drinking, or an amount measured with a standard measuring cup.
senses.example: We poured a cup of water into the bowl.

senses.definition: To make a curved shape with your hands or hold something in that shape.
senses.example: She cupped a hand around the marble so it would not fall.

senses.definition: A short slope that joins a sidewalk and a street where there would otherwise be a step.
senses.example: We rolled our wagon down the curb ramp at the corner.

senses.definition: A soft lump of milk solids that can form when milk proteins gather together.
senses.example: The cheese maker gathered the curds into a mold.

senses.definition: Something that makes an illness or problem go away.
senses.example: The book describes how scientists look for a cure.

senses.definition: To make an illness go away or make food last longer by treating it.
senses.example: The book explains how people cure some foods with salt.

senses.definition: Wanting to know or find out about something.
senses.example: I was curious about how the clock could tell time.

senses.definition: Unusual in a way that makes you wonder about it.
senses.example: There was a curious mark on the underside of the stone.

senses.definition: The kind of money used in a country or shared by several countries.
senses.example: The yen is the currency used in Japan.

senses.definition: A flow of water or air in a particular direction.
senses.example: The river current carried the leaf past the bridge.

senses.definition: The rate at which electric charge moves through a path, such as a wire.
senses.example: When the switch closes, electric current can flow through the bulb.

senses.definition: Happening, used, or true now.
senses.example: The current plan is to meet after lunch.

senses.definition: A hanging piece of cloth that can cover a window or hide part of a stage.
senses.example: The curtain opened, and the first actor stepped forward.

senses.definition: A line or shape that bends smoothly.
senses.example: Trace the curve along the edge of the bowl.

senses.definition: To bend or follow a line that bends smoothly.
senses.example: The road curves around the hill.

senses.definition: Someone who buys goods or services from a person or business.
senses.example: Each customer chose one piece of fruit.

senses.definition: To split or remove something with a sharp edge.
senses.example: Please cut the paper along the dotted line.

senses.definition: To make an amount smaller or leave part of something out.
senses.example: We had to cut one scene from the play.

senses.definition: An opening made by something sharp, or a reduction in an amount.
senses.example: There was a small cut in the corner of the paper.

senses.definition: Using digital devices or online services to bully someone, such as by sending cruel or embarrassing messages.
senses.example: I showed a grown-up what had happened so we could report the cyberbullying.

senses.definition: A shape with two matching flat ends that are parallel, like the round ends of a can, joined by a side surface.
senses.example: The rolled-up poster formed a hollow cylinder.
